subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Steam-Powered Carriages
description: A short lesson to help you apply Steam-Powered Carriages.

hook.text: Before gasoline cars, people tried to move carriages with steam—starting in the 1700s.

buildup.text: Nicolas-Joseph Cugnot built a steam tricycle in 1769. It could haul cannons for the French army.

discovery.text: Steam cars actually worked, but they were heavy, slow to start, and needed constant water refills.

twist.text: Britain's Red Flag Act of 1865 required someone to walk ahead of any car waving a red flag.

climax.text: That law killed British steam car innovation for 30 years, letting Germany and France leap ahead.

punchline.text: Bad regulation can stall progress for decades.

quiz.question: What did the Red Flag Act require?
options: A person walking ahead of the car
Cars to stay below 5 mph only
Steam engines to be banned entirely
